The {{Nihongo|'''Chichibu Shrine'''|秩父神社|Chichibu-jinja|qq=}} is a Japanese [[Shinto shrine]] at [[Chichibu, Saitama|Chichibu]] in [[Saitama Prefecture]].<ref name="kotodamaya">Kotodamaya.com, [http://www.kotodamaya.com/chichibu-jinja/ "Chichibu Jinja"]; retrieved 2013-1-26.</ref>
==History==
According to text in the ''Sendai Kuji Hongi'' (''[[Kujiki]]''), Chichibuhiko-no-mikoto, the tenth-generation descendant of the [[Kuni no miyatsuko]] of [[Chichibu Province]], established the shrine in the tenth year of [[Emperor Sujin]] to worship [[Omoikane|Yagokoro-omoikane-no-mikoto]].
The shrine contains
* {{Nihongo|[[Omoikane|Yagokoroomoikane no mikoto]]|八意思兼命|||qq=}}<ref name="kotodamaya"/>
* {{Nihongo|[[:en:Chichibuhiko no mikoto|Chichibuhiko no mikoto]]|知知夫彦命|||qq=}}<ref name="kotodamaya"/>
* {{Nihongo|[[Ame-no-Minakanushi]]-no-kami|天之御中主神|||qq=}}<ref name="kotodamaya"/>
* {{Nihongo|[[:en:Prince Chichibu|Prince Chichibu]]|秩父宮雍仁親王|Chichibu-no-Miya Yasuhito-shinnō||qq=}}<ref name="kotodamaya"/>
During the [[Kamakura period]], the shrine merged with a neighboring temple, and was known as Myōken-gū until the separation of Shinto and Buddhism (''[[Shinbutsu bunri]]'') in the late-19th century.<ref>[http://www.chichibu-jinja.or.jp/saijin/index.htm  社殿 ご由緒 at Chichibu-jinja.or.jp]; retrieved 2013-1-26.</ref>
In the [[Edo period]], it was one of 34 sacred sites of the old Chichibu Province<ref>Harold Bolitho. (2003). [https://books.google.com/books?id=OksPvlsQOZEC&dq=chichibu+province&pg=PA40  "Tokugawa Japan's Tourist Revolution,"] ''Treasures of the Yenching: Seventy-fifth Anniversary of the Harvard-Yenching Library,'' p. 40.</ref> or [[Chichibu District]].<ref>[http://www.sainokuni-kanko.jp/eng/sightseeingspot/017.html  "Chichibu Shrine" at Sainokuni-kanko.jp] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130919161424/http://www.sainokuni-kanko.jp/eng/sightseeingspot/017.html |date=2013-09-19 |qq=}}; retrieved 2013-1-26.</ref>
In the [[Meiji era]] it took the name Chichbu Shrine, with the characters 知知夫神社 appearing on the tablet of the ''[[torii]]''.
In the system of Ranked Shinto shrines, Chichibu was listed among the 3rd class of nationally significant shrines or {{nihongo|''[[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社|qq=}}.<ref>[[Richard Ponsonby-Fane|Ponsonby-Fane, Richard]]. (1963). ''The vicissitudes of Shinto,'' p. 288.</ref>
The shrine's grounds include a number of subsidiary shrines. A [[Tenmangū|Tenjin Shrine]], [[Tōshō-gū]], and a [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Shrine]] are among them.
==Events==
[[File:ChichibuFes1.jpg|thumb|Chichibu's annual night festival]]
The shrine hosts a number of events. The rice-planting festival takes place annually on April 4. The mid-summer Kawase Festival is celebrated on July 19 and 20. The Banba-machi Suwa Shrine festival is not annual, but occasional. It resembles the [[Onbashira]] festival of the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]].
Chichibu's annual night festival draws the biggest crowds. Celebrated in December, it spans the first six days of the month. The parading of floats is listed as part of the national cultural heritage.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/bsys/searchlist.asp 国指定文化財　データベース:検索結果一覧] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319233125/http://www.bunka.go.jp/bsys/searchlist.asp |date=2012-03-19 |qq=}} Retrieved August 23, 2008</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/bsys/maindetails.asp 国指定文化財] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080730003006/http://www.bunka.go.jp/bsys/maindetails.asp |date=2008-07-30 |qq=}}　データベース
:主情報詳細 秩父祭屋台 Retrieved August 23, 2008</ref>
The national government has also recognized the shrine's sacred dance (''[[kagura]]'') as an important cultural asset.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/bsys/maindetails.asp 国指定文化財　データベース:主情報詳細] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080730003006/http://www.bunka.go.jp/bsys/maindetails.asp |date=2008-07-30 |qq=}} 秩父神社神楽 Retrieved on August 23, 2008</ref> Similar honors have been awarded to its festival music, the floats, buildings and other possessions.
